title: Only Protectionism Can Safeguard European Industry
gist: Drawing a direct line from China's 2001 WTO accession to the hollowing-out of US manufacturing and the rise of Trump-style populism, the author argues Europe faces a similar fate unless it embraces tariffs against a flood of Chinese exports, since Beijing shows little sign of rebalancing its economy.

themes.theme: China trade shock 2.0, this time for Europe

insights.claim: China's 2001 accession to the World Trade Organization had consequences for the United States that few could have predicted, contributing to the hollowing out of the US manufacturing sector and a decline in manufacturing employment.
insights.speaker: Desmond Lachman
insights.so_what: Establishes the historical 'China shock' precedent that the author uses to argue for pre-emptive EU tariff action rather than repeating the US's reactive experience.
insights.quote: Few could have predicted the consequences China’s 2001 accession to the World Trade Organization would have for the United States. By contributing to the hollowing out of the US manufacturing sector and the decline in US manufacturing employment
insights.locator: paragraph beginning “WASHINGTON, DC—Few could have predicted”

insights.claim: The hollowing-out of US manufacturing from Chinese import competition helped prepare the ground for the right-wing economic populism that propelled Donald Trump's political rise.
insights.speaker: Desmond Lachman
insights.so_what: Frames Chinese import competition as a root cause of US political populism, a causal chain investors can apply when assessing how EU import competition from China could similarly fuel European populist politics.
insights.quote: China’s integration into the global economy helped prepare the ground for the right-wing economic populism that propelled Donald Trump’s political rise.
insights.locator: paragraph beginning “WASHINGTON, DC—Few could have predicted”

insights.claim: Unless Europe acts soon to protect its manufacturing sector from surging Chinese imports, it may face a fate similar to the US manufacturing decline and its political fallout.
insights.speaker: Desmond Lachman
insights.so_what: A direct warning that EU industrial and political stability is at risk from unchecked Chinese import growth, relevant to positioning in European industrials and to expectations of EU trade-policy escalation.
insights.quote: Unless Europe acts soon to protect its manufacturing sector from surging Chinese imports, it may face a similar fate.
insights.locator: paragraph beginning “WASHINGTON, DC—Few could have predicted”

insights.claim: While economic rebalancing by China toward domestic consumption would benefit everyone, Chinese leaders have given little indication that they are moving decisively in that direction.
insights.speaker: Desmond Lachman
insights.so_what: Signals skepticism that Beijing will self-correct its export-led growth model, implying persistent surplus pressure on trade partners and reduced likelihood of a near-term consumption-led rebalancing trade.
insights.quote: While economic rebalancing by China would be good for everyone, Chinese leaders have given little indication that they are moving decisively in this direction.

insights.claim: With China's ever-increasing exports threatening to decimate European manufacturing, the EU has little choice but to embrace tariffs.
insights.speaker: Desmond Lachman
insights.so_what: The author's central policy recommendation — watch for EU tariff escalation against Chinese goods as a base case, with implications for EU-China trade tensions and Chinese export-sector margins.
insights.quote: With China's ever-increasing exports threatening to decimate European manufacturing, the EU has little choice but to embrace tariffs.
